key_insight: A guided diffusion model can reconstruct physically realistic bubbly-flow velocity fields from phase-limited 2D measurements, including the hard-to-observe bubble phase.
engineering_relevance: This offers a promising generative prior for recovering missing multiphase flow data in experiments and simulations where only sparse, partial, or phase-specific measurements are available.
method: Train on 2D slices extracted from fully resolved 3D DNS of buoyancy-driven bubbly flows
Use a guided diffusion model to generate velocity fields unconditionally or conditioned on surrounding liquid-phase flow
Apply simple patching of adjacent slices to extend reconstruction toward 3D flow inside bubbles
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the reconstructed bubble-phase fields reproduce key statistical features and that slice patching yields a reasonable 3D reconstruction inside a bubble.
watch_item: Performance may depend on training data coverage and the simplicity of the slice-patching approach, so generalization to other regimes or noisier experimental measurements is not yet guaranteed.
paper_title: Gappy Reconstruction of Bubbly Flows by Guided Diffusion Models
